main_text.p: tò ex Lützelburgicis, qvintò ex Hungaris, sextò ex Polonis, septimò ex Austriacis, penes qvos hodieq; Imperium manet.
Transylvania peculiarem Tran-sylva-niæ Princi-patus Principatum constituit.

Primus Transylvaniæ Princeps fuit Stephanus Bathorius, postea Poloniæ Rex. - Deinde Principatus pervenit ad Bethlehemum Gaborem; ab hoc ad Georgium Ragotzi, cujus filius Georgius Ragotzi II, deinceps Principatum obtinuit; in cujus locum Turcarum Imperator A. C. 1657. Achatium Barckzai, & eo interemto Michaelem Apafi, posuit, qvi adhuc hodiè Turcici Imperatoris protectione gubernat.

page.notes: The printed text in the margin reads "Tran / sylva- / niæ / Princi- / patus" over several lines; it is transcribed as one note with its hyphens. The "Canon 2." line is a numbered canon and is therefore a paragraph, not a heading. The long s has been normalised to s throughout. Some word endings in the italic names (Barckzai, Gaborem) are faint in the scan and are copied as they appear.
